chunks: Al-Sakuni narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers, from 'Ali عليه السلام, who said:
"Whatever the tax collector takes from you and places in his container counts as part of your zakat. Whatever he does not place in the container, then do not count it as part of your zakat."

key_terms.الْعَاشِرُ: the collector who takes levy or tithe from people
key_terms.تَحْسُبْهُ: consider it or count it legally
key_terms.زَكَاتِكَ: your zakat obligation due from your wealth
key_terms.كُوزِهِ: his vessel or container used for collection

ai.seo_question: When does wealth taken by a tax collector count as part of my zakat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about what may be counted toward one's zakat when an official collector takes wealth. Only what the collector formally places into his collection vessel is considered part of the discharged zakat, while anything not properly entered into collection is not counted.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1613 - Al-Sakuni narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers, from Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) who said:
"Whatever the tax collector takes from you and places in his container counts as part of your Zakat. However, whatever he does not place in the container should not be counted as part of your Zakat."
